statement: The system shall comply with all relevant federal and state laws and regulations regarding the handling of controlled substances.
The system shall allow the prescriber to compose and check the content of a controlled substance prescription.
The system shall process prescription signing and transmission requests within 5 seconds for 95% of concurrent prescribers.
The system shall be designed with a modular architecture to facilitate updates and maintenance.
The system shall be compatible with multiple electronic health information systems and pharmacy applications.
The system shall provide clear and concise instructions for prescribers to follow when signing controlled substance prescriptions.
The system shall comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) standards for electronic health information.
The system shall digitally sign and archive the signed controlled substance prescription record.
The system shall transmit the signed controlled substance prescription to the pharmacy.
The system shall maintain an internal audit trail with daily analysis and incident reporting.
The system shall allow the prescriber to cancel or change an existing controlled substance prescription.
The system shall provide a warning to the prescriber if there are any allergies or drug interactions with the prescribed controlled substance.
The system shall retain all archived records electronically for at least two years from the date of their receipt or creation.
The system shall ensure that the prescriber's authentication credentials are not shared or reused by unauthorized individuals.
The system shall maintain a backup of controlled substance prescription records daily.
The system shall enforce role-based access control to ensure that only authorized personnel can access controlled substance prescription records.
The system shall ensure the integrity of controlled substance prescription records by verifying the digital signature upon receipt.
The system shall prompt the prescriber to authenticate using a two-factor authentication protocol before signing a controlled substance prescription.
